title: Contextual Distributionally Robust Chance-Constrained Programs: Exact Reformulations and Valid Inequalities
summary: We study a contextual distributionally robust chance-constrained programming (C-DRCCP) model that controls violation probabilities conditional on a neighborhood of a target context. The ambiguity set is defined over the joint distribution of contexts and outcomes using the Wasserstein distance. For affine safety systems with right-hand-side uncertainty, we derive an exact mixed-integer programming (MIP) reformulation.
